segments.text: When does calldata cost 64 gas per byte, and when does a normal call still pay 4 and 16?
On Glamsterdam, little work means 64 for every byte, zero or not. Fusaka stays at 10 and 40.
These are one hundred zero bytes, and the call does no work. The floor is six thousand four hundred.
The floor is one thousand. Ten gas per zero byte.
Now every byte is nonzero. The floor still wins. Forty becomes sixty-four, not ten.
A few hundred additions. That work costs more than the floor, so each byte stays at sixteen.
No calldata here. An address and a storage key still pay sixty-four each on Glamsterdam.
Little work, sixty-four a byte. Real work, four and sixteen. Fusaka stays at ten and forty.
The floor schedule is on Forkcast. The four shapes are on feelyourprotocol dot org.
